missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend whey unless allergy status and product composition are clarified by a qualified clinician/allergist; do not assume lactose-free means milk-protein-free.
safety_exclusions: Do not confuse milk-protein allergy with lactose intolerance.
Do not rely solely on 'lactose-free' or marketing claims to establish allergen safety.
Do not recommend a product with undeclared or uncertain milk-protein content.
professional_escalation_conditions: Prior anaphylaxis, respiratory symptoms, angioedema or systemic reaction to milk.
Any suspected allergic reaction after exposure; emergency symptoms require urgent care.
population_and_context: People reporting milk-protein allergy who are considering whey protein; whey is milk-derived and may contain allergenic milk proteins.
dose_constraints: No dose; whey is not appropriate as a default recommendation in confirmed milk-protein allergy.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS exercise fact sheet identifies whey as a milk-derived protein source; allergen risk and product labeling must be assessed against the actual ingredient list and applicable food-allergen rules.
